LMGTE.title: Gulf Porsche takes LMGTE by a lap as AF Corse loses two Ferraris
LMGTE.dek: Wainwright, Carroll and Keen won LMGTE in the Gulf Racing UK Porsche, a lap clear of JMW’s Ferrari, after both AF Corse works Ferraris from the front rows retired.

facts.v: Rugolo’s 2:00.151 put the #81 AF Corse Ferrari on class pole, 0.118s clear of Bachler’s Proton Porsche.

one.label: Sportscar365: Greaves on Pole for ELMS Season Opener

facts.v: The Gulf Porsche was waved past the safety car to rejoin behind the overall leader, which gave it almost a lap on the chasing JMW Ferrari.

facts.v: The MarcVDS BMW Z4 GTE was handed a stop-go penalty late on for passing under the safety car, which ended its chance of a podium on its European debut.

chapters.title: Nine cars, six of them Ferraris
text: Nine cars made up the LMGTE field for the opening round, and Ferrari supplied six of them: three AF Corse entries (#51, #55 and #81) plus those of Formula Racing, AT Racing and JMW Motorsport. Porsche 911 RSRs came from Gulf Racing UK and Proton Competition, while BMW Team MarcVDS brought the Z4 GTE to European racing for the first time, with Priaulx, Hassid and Krohn sharing the #52. Gulf had a single GTE car this year, with Goethe committed to the World Endurance Championship in an Aston Martin.

Practice was untidy. AF Corse Ferraris were fastest in the first session, Aguas setting a 2:02.428 in the #81, with the BMW third. In the second the #56 AT Racing Ferrari went quickest on a 2:01.248, ahead of Bachler’s Proton Porsche and Priaulx, the only three cars in the 2:01s. Peter Mann put the #51 into the gravel twice, the first excursion bringing a brief red flag. Al Qubaisi’s Proton Porsche was left stranded after a clash with the BMW at the final corner, and the Gulf Porsche and the #55 Ferrari got in each other’s way in the pit lane.

chapters.title: Rugolo takes pole at the death
text: Bachler set the early marker for Proton and it stood until the last minutes, when Rugolo found a clear lap and took the #81 AF Corse Ferrari to pole with a 2:00.151, 0.118s ahead of the Porsche. Pier Guidi was third for AT Racing on a 2:00.478, despite spinning on his final attempt, and Priaulx’s BMW was fourth on 2:00.480, two thousandths further back.

Carroll put the Gulf Porsche fifth, then came Tordoff in the #66 JMW Ferrari, Griffin in the #55, Giammaria in the #51 and Mac in the #60 Formula Racing car. The grid therefore placed the eventual winner and runner-up fifth and sixth in class.

chapters.title: Gulf takes over
text: The #81 Ferrari led from pole, but lost the class lead when it ended up in the gravel at Turn 1. That handed the class to Keen in the Gulf Porsche, with Scott’s #55 Ferrari second after getting past the JMW car, which was then also passed by Cressoni in the #51.

The BMW spun with steam coming from under the bonnet and dropped to the back of the class, and the #56 AT Racing Ferrari also went off on its own. Once the first round of stops was complete, Ried led in the Proton Porsche.

chapters.title: Both works Ferraris out
text: AF Corse’s #81 and #51 were both out before half distance, after 32 and 35 laps, which left the team with only the #55 in the class. Wainwright was leading the Gulf Porsche by more than 40 seconds from Richardson in the JMW Ferrari, but the gap was shrinking quickly when the safety car appeared with around an hour and a half left.

The neutralisation reshuffled the class: Gulf came out of it with a cushion of almost a lap over the JMW car, a lead that held to the flag. The BMW, having rejoined at the back of the class, was climbing the order.

chapters.title: JMW chases, BMW climbs
text: Jesse Krohn took the BMW to third early in the last hour, but the car was shuffled back to fourth in the closing stages. JMW kept up the chase and moved from sixth on the grid to second, while Griffin brought the #55 Ferrari home in third.

chapters.title: Carroll takes the flag
text: Carroll took the Gulf Porsche across the line to win LMGTE, with Tordoff’s JMW Ferrari second, 23.439s ahead of the #55 Ferrari. Gulf was the only car on the lead lap; the #66, #55, #52, #88 and #60 all completed 109 laps to the winner’s 110.

chapters.title: Gulf opens its season with a win
text: Wainwright, Carroll and Keen opened the season with the class win in the #86 Gulf Racing UK Porsche. George Richardson, Robert Smith and Samuel Tordoff were second for JMW, with Duncan Cameron, Matt Griffin and Aaron Scott third for AF Corse; Griffin also set the class fastest lap, a 2:01.772.

The MarcVDS BMW of Priaulx, Hassid and Krohn took fourth on its European debut, ahead of the Proton Porsche, the #60 Formula Racing Ferrari and, three laps down, the #56 AT Racing Ferrari. Of the AF Corse trio, only the #55 finished. The championship moves to Imola in May.

GTC.title: TDS BMW wins GTC by two laps in a race of attrition
GTC.dek: Perera, Lunardi and Dermont led TDS Racing’s BMW Z4 GT3 to a two-lap GTC win from pole as three of the six cars failed to finish.

facts.v: Perera’s 2:01.939 was more than a second faster than the best of the AF Corse Ferraris.

chapters.title: Six cars and a Dunlop switch
text: GTC came to Silverstone much reduced. Six cars lined up after a drop in numbers that followed complaints about Balance of Performance in 2014, with three AF Corse Ferrari 458 Italia GT3s (#62, #63 and #64) facing one each of BMW, Aston Martin and Lamborghini. TDS Racing ran the Z4 GT3 (#59) for Perera, Lunardi and Dermont alongside its LMP2 programme. Massive Motorsport, an all-Danish squad, was new to the series with an Aston Martin Vantage GT3 for Elgaard, Poulsen and Moller, and Gulf Racing UK fielded a Lamborghini Gallardo for Goethe, Brown and Hamilton.

Both GT classes now ran on Dunlop control tyres, replacing the Michelins GTC used in 2014. In practice the TDS BMW topped the first session on a 2:03.082, around seven tenths clear of the #63 Ferrari. The second session was led by AF Corse, Cioci’s #63 and Hall’s #62 separated by six thousandths, with the TDS BMW only a tenth behind.

chapters.title: Perera more than a second clear
text: AF Corse held the first three places early, Cioci’s #63 setting a 2:03.807, with Brown briefly third for Gulf’s Lamborghini. Perera then took the TDS BMW to pole with a 2:01.939, more than a second faster than the next car, Cioci’s Ferrari on 2:03.002.

Castellacci’s #62 was third on 2:03.298 and Guedes’s #64 fourth on 2:03.564, ahead of Elgaard’s Aston Martin (2:04.046) and Brown’s Lamborghini (2:04.596). Massive Motorsport had a troubled session, including a big off at Luffield.

chapters.title: Aston Martin leads, one Ferrari never starts
text: The #62 AF Corse Ferrari was out before the race was under way and ended as not classified. Elgaard took the Aston Martin to the head of the class before its first stop and still led afterwards, with the #63 Ferrari second and Goethe improving steadily in the Gulf Lamborghini.

chapters.title: TDS takes control
text: By the middle of the race Lunardi had the TDS BMW in front by nine seconds over Roda’s #63 Ferrari, with Hamilton’s Lamborghini back in third.

That order changed with about an hour and a half left. The Aston Martin had slowed to avoid a faster prototype and, with the car on the marbles at Woodcote, Roda’s Ferrari ran into the back of it and spun it into the wall. Both cars were out of the race, the #63 after 67 laps and the #68 after 65, and the safety car came out. The #64 Ferrari, now in second, would not lose the place.

chapters.title: Positions pegged
text: The order did not change in the final hour. TDS Racing’s BMW stayed two laps clear of Rasmussen, Barreiros and Guedes in the #64 Ferrari, and Hamilton drove the Gulf Lamborghini to the flag for third.

chapters.title: Two laps clear
text: Perera, Lunardi and Dermont took the TDS BMW across the line with 108 laps completed, two clear of the #64 Ferrari. The Gulf Lamborghini was third on 92 laps, 16 behind the winner.

chapters.title: TDS wins from pole
text: TDS Racing won GTC from pole, with Perera also setting the class fastest lap, a 2:03.594. AF Corse’s #64 (Rasmussen, Barreiros, Guedes) was second, and Gulf Racing UK’s Lamborghini (Goethe, Brown, Hamilton) took the last podium place in a race of attrition: the #63, #68 and #62 did not finish.
The next round of the championship is at Imola in May.

LMP3.title: Team LNT takes a one-two in LMP3’s first race
LMP3.dek: Hoy and Robertson led Team LNT’s Ginetta to victory in the first ELMS LMP3 race, a lap clear of Simpson and Paletou, after Robertson took pole.

facts.v: Robertson’s 1:59.892 was the first lap under two minutes by an LMP3 car and faster than every GT runner.

chapters.title: A new class arrives
text: LMP3 made its debut in the European Le Mans Series with five Ginetta-Nissans on Michelin control tyres. Team LNT brought two: the #3 for Chris Hoy, the Olympic great stepping into prototypes, and Charlie Robertson, and the #2 for factory driver Michael Simpson and Nissan GT Academy winner Gaetan Paletou. Team RLR and the University of Bolton ran the #7 for Rob Garofall and Jens Petersen, Lanan Racing the #11 for Craven, Hollings and Foster, and SVK by Speed Factory the #15 for Calko, Fuster and Matijosaitis.

Delivery delays had cost the cars track time, and teams would be able to drop their lowest result in a season in which four of the five rounds count. In the first practice session only four cars ran, the #15 staying in the garage, and Garofall set the fastest time with a lap in the 2:04s. The second session brought big improvements, with Robertson down to 2:01.869 and Simpson a tenth off in the sister car, while the #7 lost time with power steering problems.

chapters.title: LNT one-two, quicker than every GT car
text: Robertson took pole for Team LNT with a 1:59.892, the first sub-two-minute lap in the class, which was quicker than any GT car and put him 12th overall. Simpson made it a one-two for the team with a 2:00.457 in the #2.
Lanan’s #11 was third on 2:02.045, ahead of the University of Bolton car on 2:02.686. SVK’s #15 was last, a 2:06.697, after going off and hitting the barriers at Stowe.

chapters.title: Robertson into the lead
text: Robertson had taken the class lead from Hollings’s Lanan car within the first 18 minutes after a fast climb through the field and went on to build a lead of more than 20 seconds. By the end of the hour Team LNT held the first two places, with the #7 car, now with Petersen, third.

chapters.title: Hoy in front
text: The Lanan car was first to meet real trouble, sitting in the pits at half distance, and it was out after 52 laps. Chris Hoy now had the lead car and was a lap up on Simpson in the #2, handing back to Robertson with a gap of over a minute. Garofall took second place for the #7 while Paletou took over the #2.

chapters.title: Four still running
text: With four cars still running, Robertson took the final stint of the lead Ginetta and resumed with a lead of over a minute on the sister LNT car.

chapters.title: LNT first and second
text: Robertson took the chequered flag after 107 laps, with the #2 LNT Ginetta one lap behind and the University of Bolton car on 105 laps in third.

chapters.title: LMP3 gets off the ground
text: Hoy and Robertson won the class on its debut, ahead of Simpson and Paletou, with Garofall and Petersen third for Team RLR and the University of Bolton. SVK by Speed Factory’s Calko, Fuster and Matijosaitis finished fourth on 102 laps, five behind the winners. Robertson also set the class fastest lap, a 2:01.214.
Four of the five cars finished their first race, and the class goes to Imola in May.
